title: Personal Portfolio Website
details:
Overview


This project is a custom-built personal portfolio website designed as a living system rather than a static page. It serves as both a public-facing professional profile and a private content management platform, allowing the site to evolve continuously without repeated code changes.


Motivation


Traditional portfolios and resumes are static snapshots that quickly become outdated and require manual edits to maintain. I wanted a system that could grow with my career, reflect ongoing work, and reduce the friction involved in updating content.


Instead of treating the portfolio as a one-time deliverable, I approached it as an engineering problem: how to design a maintainable, extensible system for presenting professional information.


Design Philosophy


The website was intentionally designed around the following principles:



  • Separation between content and presentation



  • Minimal friction for updates and iteration



  • Clean, distraction-free public interface



  • Private control over what is visible and when



The goal was to build something I could actively use, not just showcase.


Key Features



  • Public portfolio with sections for experience, projects, skills, and education



  • Password-protected admin panel for content management



  • Ability to add, edit, reorder, and hide sections without modifying source files



  • Support for images and structured project entries



  • Hosted via GitHub Pages for simplicity and reliability



Technical Implementation


The site is built using standard web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) with a custom admin interface layered on top. The admin panel enables dynamic updates to the site content while keeping the public-facing pages lightweight and fast.


This approach allows the website to function as a personal content system rather than a static document, while remaining fully client-side and easy to deploy.


What This Project Demonstrates


This project reflects my broader engineering approach:



  • Treating personal workflows as systems worth designing



  • Reducing repetitive effort through tooling



  • Valuing clarity, maintainability, and long-term usability


While simple in appearance, the site is structured to support continuous iteration as my work and experience grow.

title: GridPlot
details:
Overview


GridPlot is a custom Python-based data visualization and analysis tool developed to support R&D testing workflows involving large, heterogeneous datasets. It was built to reduce friction between data collection, analysis, and engineering decision making during rapid iteration cycles.


Background and Motivation


During R&D testing, data was generated across multiple test runs, sensors, locations, and configurations, typically stored in CSV or Excel files. Existing tools were either too rigid, required repetitive manual preprocessing, or were poorly suited for quick comparisons across datasets. As testing progressed, the lack of a flexible, repeatable analysis workflow became a bottleneck.


The need was not for another generic plotting script, but for a practical analysis workbench that allowed engineers to explore data, test hypotheses, and extract insights quickly without rewriting code for every new dataset.


Design Goals


The primary goals behind GridPlot were:



  • Enable fast exploration of test data without heavy preprocessing



  • Support multiple data sources and test runs in a single view



  • Allow derived metrics and transformations without modifying raw data



  • Make analysis repeatable and easy to revisit



  • Keep the tool simple enough for daily use during testing cycles



Key Capabilities


GridPlot allows users to load multiple spreadsheet files simultaneously and treat each dataset as an independent layer. For each layer, users can:



  • Plot direct columns or define derived expressions



  • Apply scaling and offsets per dataset



  • Compare multiple datasets on a common axis



  • Visualize data spreads (min, max, median) to understand variation



  • Perform spatial indexing and aggregation for survey-style datasets



To support real-world testing workflows, session persistence was implemented, allowing complete analysis states to be saved and restored. This significantly reduced setup time when revisiting past tests or comparing results across locations and iterations.


Technical Implementation


The application is built in Python with a desktop GUI using PyQt. Interactive visualizations are rendered using Plotly, enabling responsive exploration of large datasets. While AI-assisted tools were used to accelerate code development and refinement, the overall architecture, feature set, and workflows were driven entirely by observed engineering constraints and practical testing needs.


Impact and Learnings


GridPlot helped streamline data analysis during testing by making insights easier to access and comparisons faster to perform. More importantly, it reflects a broader engineering approach: identifying friction in workflows, abstracting the core problem, and building tools that improve clarity, learning speed, and decision quality.


Although initially developed as an internal utility, parts of the tool continue to support ongoing analysis workflows, reinforcing the value of building lightweight, purpose-driven engineering tools.

title: National CFD Competition
details:
National CFD Championship (SAE India) | 2nd Place

Simulation Analyst – Team "Misfits"

"Achieving national-level precision through computational efficiency and physics-led optimization."


Project Overview

A 6-month national competition organized by SAE India, spanning from advanced CFD workshops at TKMCE to a 48-hour final "Sprint" in Chennai. The challenge involved multi-physics simulations, including internal pipe flows, wind turbine aerodynamics, and complex Conjugate Heat Transfer (CHT).


Technical Execution & Strategy

  • Hardware Constraint as an Asset: While competing against high-performance workstations, I utilized an entry-level Intel i3 (7th Gen) system. This required a rigorous focus on Mesh Independence Studies and Local Refinement to ensure convergence and accuracy without exceeding hardware limits.
  • Multi-Physics Simulations: Conducted steady-state and transient analyses for:
  • Conjugate Heat Transfer (CHT): Thermal management of a high-density server room with multiple heat sources and ventilation inlets.
  • Fluid Dynamics: 2D/3D analysis of wind turbine profiles and pressure-driven pipe flows using Ansys Fluent.
  • Workflow Optimization: Developed a streamlined simulation pipeline that allowed our team to be the only group in the competition to achieve a 100% completion rate across all assignments ahead of schedule.

Crisis Management & Results

  • The Sprint Challenge: During a critical software-geometry anomaly in the finals, I pivoted the team’s focus to perfect the Solver Configuration and Post-Processing Logic.
  • The Result: Secured 2nd Place Nationally. The judges specifically commended our team's coordination and the superior quality of our post-processed results, noting that our methodology remained sound even under anomalous technical conditions.
  • Validation: Post-competition, I verified the logic by re-solving the final problem, confirming that the methodology was 100% accurate and capable of producing high-fidelity thermal contours.

title: Spend Tracker
details:
Overview


An experimental Android utility engineered to solve the primary failure mode of personal finance tools: logging friction. Built as a personal daily driver through rapid prototyping with Google AI Studio ("vibe coding"), the app focuses entirely on minimizing the interaction cost of recording expenses.


The Problem


Most expense trackers fail because manual logging demands too many steps: unlocking the phone, launching an app, navigating menus, and filling out multiple form fields. Over time, tracking fatigue leads to abandoned consistency.


System Architecture & Key Features


To test different friction-reduction mechanics, two distinct modes were implemented:


  • Passive Event-Driven Capture: Monitors payment notifications to trigger an instant floating confirmation overlay, or automatically parses vendor and transaction amounts directly from notification data.


  • Hardware-Triggered Privacy Mode (Assist Intent): For users who prefer complete privacy without granting notification-reading permissions, the app hooks into the Android Assist intent. Long-pressing the power button (or assistant gesture) immediately summons a lightweight 2-field popup (amount + category) that dismisses in under two seconds.


Rapid Prototyping with Google AI Studio


Rather than hand-writing boilerplate Android scaffolding, I leveraged Google AI Studio for rapid "vibe coding" iteration:


  • Iteratively explored Android system hooks (NotificationListenerService, Assist intents, and overlay window management).


  • Focused effort on low-latency UI ergonomics and instant-entry popups rather than distribution overhead.


Key Takeaway


Validated that reducing interaction cost from ~15 seconds to sub-2-seconds dramatically sustains habit tracking. Serves as a working demonstration of pragmatic UX and AI-augmented rapid tool building.

title: Atomic Habits
details:
Overview


An experimental native Android habit system designed around the behavioral psychology principles of James Clear's Atomic Habits. Rather than functioning as a passive checklist, the app explores how mobile operating system capabilities—specifically contextual location awareness and home-screen widgets—can reduce psychological friction in habit formation.


Core Behavioral Concepts & Features


  • Location-Triggered Cues (Geofencing): Habits are heavily influenced by environment. Using Android's LocationServices and GeofenceBroadcastReceiver, the app delivers contextual nudges when entering specific physical environments (e.g., gym, office, library).


  • Frictionless Home Screen Widget: Built custom Android app widgets (HabitWidgetProvider & StackView) allowing instant glanceability and single-tap completions directly from the launcher without opening the full app.


  • Daily Focus & Reflection: Replaces guilt-inducing streak breaks with a structured Today queue and a reflection journal interface to diagnose why habits stall.


Technical Stack & Architecture


  • Language & UI: 100% Kotlin with modern declarative Jetpack Compose and Material 3 design tokens.


  • Architecture: Unidirectional Data Flow (UDF) / MVVM with HabitViewModel and Kotlin Coroutines/Flow.


  • Local Persistence: Offline-first architecture using Room database (AppDatabase, HabitDao, HabitRepository).


  • AI Integration: Integrated with the Gemini API for adaptive reflection prompts and habit coaching insights.


Project Status & Learnings


Kept as an experimental architectural prototype to validate geofence-triggered intent and widget-first UX. Serves as a direct exploration of translating behavioral psychology into native mobile software.
